text:
sasha: heads-up — seeing serial console packet corruption on ~30 nodes in us-central1 after last BMC image roll. provisioner latency +5m on boots.
lee: ack. was that the secure-boot toggle patch? noticed a few consoles drop.
maria: can you paste the rollout id? ops-bot alerted earlier.
sasha: rollout id bmc-secboot-v2, group r-cc-12, started 02:13 UTC. logs show repeated 'UART parity error' and 'IPMI session reset'.
lee: oof. scheduler shows 12 GPU pods evicted from that rack, a couple hit reserved fallback.
ops-bot: Rollout update: bmc-secboot-v2 -> 30/320 nodes healthy; 6 failing; auto-rollback policy triggered (attempt 1).
maria: pinging firmware team in #eng-firmware, can we rollback manually if auto fails?
deploy-bot: rollback job queued for bmc-secboot-v2 -> priority=high. ETA 18m.
sasha: quick triage shows UART FIFO underruns on SOC when secureboot flag toggles during SMM handoff. hypothesis: pinmux goes low-power and drops serial frames.
lee: that would explain corrupted console output and provisioner retries. any node-level workaround?
sasha: temp workaround: disable serial multiplexing on jump hosts and force ipmi reset. runs helped a few nodes. snippet: ```for n in $(cat bad-nodes.txt); do ipmitool -I lanplus -H $n -U admin -P $IPMI_PASS mc reset cold; done```
maria: thanks — we should also throttle provisioner parallelism for that rack to reduce concurrent IPMI storms.
lee: doing that now — set provisioner.max_concurrent=8 for r-cc-12.
jon: cost heads-up: evictions + job restarts are already adding up. rough estimate so far $480 in preemptible churn. if this hits reserved scale-ups, could be ~$1.6k. tagging finance.
sasha: revert started at 02:34 UTC, ops-bot reports rollback completed at 02:37. nodes transitioned to provisioning; some require manual console reattach (5 nodes).
maria: monitoring cluster health and GPU allocation. moved a few long-running jobs to us-west1 to reduce SLA pressure.
lee: manual console attaches in progress. one node had corrupted UEFI environment; had to reflash BMC cert store.
sasha: firmware acknowledged bug: secureboot toggle also updated a PMIC register that changes UART bus voltage. they've paused the next canary and will push a patch that preserves UART PMIC state.
maria: action items: [1] hold canary; [2] require UART continuity test in firmware CI; [3] add ipmi-session-backoff in provisioner; [4] postmortem if rollback >6h.
jon: ops/internal-billing follow-up scheduled. assigning to @jon for chargeback review.
lee: will update rollout playbook to include netboot/serial fallback checklist and add compatibility matrix for BMC fw vs hypervisor versions.
sasha: closing loop — will verify all nodes healthy by 06:00 UTC then close incident. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Incident closed at 05:58 UTC. rollback_reason: uart-fifo-underrun-on-secureboot-toggle.
jon: thanks all — open a follow-up doc in /eng-infra/runbooks for the new UART test and add a scheduled re-roll only after signed-off tests.
maria: filing the ticket and draft postmortem now.
sasha: resources: logs uploaded to s3://redwood-ops/incident/1793332222/, node list in bad-nodes.txt, ipmi debug traces attached.
lee: thumbs up.\n
